items.requirement: Define the exact production responsibility of Traditional IaC.
Document what Traditional IaC owns and explicitly does not own.
Identify upstream, downstream, and peer dependencies of Traditional IaC.
Define the authoritative source of truth used by Traditional IaC.
Document assumptions Traditional IaC makes about nodes, runtimes, networks, storage, and control planes.
Define tenant, environment, site, and workload boundaries relevant to Traditional IaC.
Separate mandatory Traditional IaC capabilities from optional optimizations.
Document unsupported deployment patterns and non-goals for Traditional IaC.
Assign an accountable owner and escalation path for Traditional IaC.
Approve an architecture decision record for Traditional IaC, its technologies (Terraform, HCL, state files, resource graphs, plan/apply), and its function (Day-1 provisioning).
Translate the source function of Traditional IaC — Day-1 provisioning — into testable SHALL-level requirements.
Define functional requirements for Traditional IaC across cloud, datacenter, near-edge, and far-edge contexts where applicable.
Define non-functional requirements for latency, availability, durability, consistency, isolation, or determinism as applicable.
Define success, partial success, degraded operation, retryable failure, and terminal failure semantics for Traditional IaC.
Define lifecycle states and legal state transitions managed or exposed by Traditional IaC.
Define versioning and backward-compatibility requirements for Traditional IaC.
Define capacity ceilings, quotas, and fairness semantics relevant to Traditional IaC.
Define behavior when network connectivity is intermittent or absent.
Define precedence rules when Traditional IaC requirements conflict with security, residency, SLO, or cost constraints.
Maintain a requirements traceability matrix from each Traditional IaC requirement to implementation and verification evidence.
Enumerate every API, WIT contract, RPC, event, file, device, hypervisor, or control-plane boundary exposed by Traditional IaC.
Use versioned typed schemas for all externally visible Traditional IaC contracts.
Define authentication requirements at each Traditional IaC boundary.
Define authorization and explicit capability requirements at each Traditional IaC boundary.
Define timeout, cancellation, retry, idempotency, and backpressure semantics for Traditional IaC.
Define structured failure codes and machine-readable error details for Traditional IaC.
Define compatibility behavior when peers use different supported versions.
Document payload, concurrency, queue, connection, or resource limits at Traditional IaC interfaces.
Provide reference examples and conformance fixtures for Traditional IaC.
Create automated integration tests proving Traditional IaC interoperates with adjacent architectural layers.
Select and pin approved implementations, versions, or specifications for Traditional IaC: Terraform, HCL, state files, resource graphs, plan/apply.
Separate immutable artifacts from mutable configuration and state for Traditional IaC.
Define declarative configuration and secure defaults for Traditional IaC.
Validate configuration before activation and fail closed on security-critical errors.
Support site- and environment-specific configuration without rebuilding immutable artifacts.
Record configuration provenance, version, author, and activation time.
Apply atomic or transactional configuration updates where partial application is unsafe.
Define automatic and operator-driven rollback for failed Traditional IaC changes.
Keep credentials and secret material out of ordinary Traditional IaC configuration and diagnostics.
Provide a deterministic bootstrap path from an empty node/environment to healthy Traditional IaC operation.
Threat-model Traditional IaC against malicious tenants, compromised workloads, hostile inputs, supply-chain compromise, and control-plane abuse.
Apply least privilege to every identity and capability used by Traditional IaC.
Eliminate ambient filesystem, network, device, kernel, and secret authority wherever Traditional IaC permits.
Authenticate nodes, peers, artifacts, providers, and control-plane actors before trust is granted.
Verify signatures, digests, provenance, and approved versions for executable or policy artifacts consumed by Traditional IaC.
Enforce tenant/workload isolation across Traditional IaC execution, memory, state, network, and device boundaries as applicable.
Encrypt sensitive Traditional IaC data in transit and at rest with managed key rotation.
Define safe behavior when identity, attestation, policy, key, or time services are unavailable.
Emit tamper-evident audit events for security-sensitive Traditional IaC operations.
Run adversarial tests for privilege escalation, injection, replay, spoofing, escape, side channels, and resource exhaustion.
Enumerate component, process, VM, node, site, network, provider, dependency, and control-plane failures affecting Traditional IaC.
Define automated health and stall detection thresholds for Traditional IaC.
Implement bounded retry with backoff and jitter only where operations are safe to retry.
Implement admission control, load shedding, or circuit breaking to prevent Traditional IaC failure cascades.
Define failover behavior without violating isolation, residency, or consistency requirements.
Provide degraded operation when noncritical dependencies are unavailable.
Define crash-consistency, restart, resume, or replay semantics for mutable Traditional IaC state.
Protect against split-brain, duplicate ownership, stale controllers, or duplicate execution where relevant.
Provide quarantine, freeze, disable, or isolation controls for unsafe Traditional IaC behavior.
Run fault-injection tests proving Traditional IaC recovery against documented objectives.
Establish reproducible baselines for Traditional IaC latency, throughput, startup, CPU, memory, storage, network, and power overhead.
Define p50, p95, p99, and worst-case performance thresholds for Traditional IaC.
Measure Traditional IaC under steady load, burst load, overload, scale-out, scale-in, and recovery.
Measure per-workload and per-tenant overhead introduced by Traditional IaC.
Identify avoidable serialization, copies, context switches, network hops, duplicated images, or duplicated state in Traditional IaC.
Apply locality, caching, direct composition, batching, zero-copy, or kernel-bypass optimizations where semantics permit.
Bound memory growth, queue depth, buffer size, concurrency, and resource fan-out.
Measure power and thermal impact on constrained edge nodes where relevant.
Define capacity models and saturation signals that predict when Traditional IaC needs more resources.
Block releases that regress approved Traditional IaC startup, density, throughput, or tail-latency thresholds.
Expose Traditional IaC health, readiness, version, configuration, dependency status, and active capability set.
Emit structured metrics for rate, errors, latency, saturation, backlog, and resource use.
Emit structured logs with stable node, tenant, workload, component, and operation identifiers.
Propagate trace context across all relevant Traditional IaC boundaries.
Expose high-cardinality diagnostic detail safely without leaking tenant or secret data.
Record the reason for every automated decision made by Traditional IaC.
Provide an operator-readable explain view linking decisions to input state, policies, topology, and constraints.
Correlate Traditional IaC events with application release lineage and the live infrastructure graph.
Define telemetry retention, sampling, privacy, and export policy.
Create dashboards and alerts distinguishing ordinary load, degradation, policy rejection, dependency failure, attack, and software defect.
Create unit tests for deterministic Traditional IaC logic and state transitions.
Create contract tests for every public Traditional IaC interface.
Create integration tests with every supported adjacent layer and execution tier.
Create compatibility tests across supported CPU architectures, runtimes, hypervisors, providers, and protocol versions relevant to Traditional IaC.
Fuzz parsers, schemas, protocol handlers, WIT/RPC boundaries, or untrusted inputs handled by Traditional IaC.
Create concurrency and race-condition tests for shared/distributed Traditional IaC state.
Create security tests derived directly from the Traditional IaC threat model.
Create benchmark, soak, burst, and fleet-scale tests appropriate to Traditional IaC.
Create disaster, partition, reconnect, and degraded-control-plane tests.
Require machine-readable acceptance evidence before certifying a Traditional IaC release for production.
Define production SLOs, error budgets, and support commitments for Traditional IaC.
Define canary, staged rollout, rollback, and emergency-disable procedures for Traditional IaC.
Maintain a supported-version compatibility matrix for Traditional IaC and adjacent dependencies.
Define patching, vulnerability response, and end-of-life SLAs for Traditional IaC.
Provide backup, restore, migration, or reconstruction procedures for Traditional IaC state where applicable.
Create day-0 bootstrap, day-1 deployment, and day-2 operation runbooks.
Define incident severity, paging, escalation, containment, and recovery procedures.
Perform recurring access, policy, dependency, configuration, and architecture reviews.
Track exceptions, waivers, technical debt, and deprecated behaviors with owners and expiry dates.
Require a formal production exit gate confirming architecture, requirements, interfaces, implementation, security, resilience, performance, observability, testing, rollback, and ownership readiness.
